messages:
maria: Heads-up — enterprise customer reported sudden 429 + increased latency on their Dedicated pool rp-512. They say traffic pattern unchanged but errors started at ~14:02 UTC. SLA alert fired.
kevin: Can you paste a sample request_id and any headers we can use to trace? Also which model and route?
maria: request_id=rid_9a8b7c, route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-3-large, pool=rp-512. Headers attached in the ticket. Customer notes responses were streamed.
joe-cs: They saw 429s mostly on streamed responses, non-streaming requests looked OK. Customer provided a curl repro.
kevin: streaming + long-lived connections can chew through concurrency tokens. Do we have the pool's concurrency cap & token-bucket settings?
devon: I pulled rp-512 config — reserved_capacity=120 qps, max_concurrency=30, burst_tokens=600, refill_rate=10/s. Looks normal.
sarah: ops-bot just posted an alert: "dedicated/pool/rp-512/penalty-window: token deficit exceeded threshold" at 14:03 UTC.
ops-bot: ALERT: pool rp-512 entered penalty window (30s) due to sustained token underflow. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming).
kevin: If streaming responses hold connections open for longer than expected, the effective concurrency footprint increases. Could be a streaming client that reads slowly causing tokens to be held. Any slow consumers?
maria: Customer said they had a small percentage of slow clients after a deploy at 13:58 UTC. They rolled back at 14:10 but the 429s persisted.
devon: I checked proxy logs: a subset of requests had keep-alive durations > 45s. Typical median is 200-400ms. So yes, long-lived streams. Also seeing many small chunk writes instead of single flushes.
kevin: That aligns — token-bucket accounted by concurrent inflight streams + token refill. Short bursts ok, but slow drains/long tails push pool into penalty window which triggers aggressive rate-limiting to protect SLO.
sarah: Customer SLA expects 99.9% p95 latency and no sustained 429s under their committed throughput. We need to show root cause and mitigation.
maria: Repro steps from customer (they provided):
---
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Pool: rp-512" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","stream":true}'
---
When they ran a small loop at 100 concurrent streams, tokens dropped quickly.
devon: Quick repro on staging: I ran 80 concurrent streaming clients with artificial slow drains (sleep 30s between chunk reads) and pool tokens depleted within ~40s, followed by 429s. Non-streaming clients at same RPS fine.
kevin: Two action items: (1) immediate customer remediation (suggested short-term): reduce concurrency per client, add backpressure client-side or temporary rate cap; (2) platform fixes / mitigations: consider adjusting burst_tokens and penalty window heuristics for streaming-heavy routes, and add per-connection idle timeout enforcement.
sarah: Also need to verify billing/usage — they were charged for streaming tokens even when 429s returned? Customer flagged potential billing break.
joe-cs: I confirmed billing shows the tokens consumed only for accepted responses. For 429s we didn't bill. I'll attach ledger rows.
maria: For on-call: can we patch a rule to prioritize canary fallback to a smaller model for streaming when pool is in penalty window? That would reduce token/time per response.
devon: Feasible — fallback policy exists but not enabled for this route. We can enable a temporary rule to route to redwood-3-medium for rp-512 when penalty active. I can flip it and monitor.
kevin: Also add a throttling advisory to the customer: set client-side max_concurrency=20 and enable chunk coalescing to ensure faster drains. Provide recommended client patch.
sarah: I'll own the customer comms and SLA remediation note. Assign follow-ups: devon to enable fallback + telemetry, kevin to draft long-term tuning plan (burst/refill/penalty), maria to coordinate customer rollback verification, joe-cs to confirm billing rows.
maria: timeline: devon will enable fallback in 15m, we'll monitor for 10m, then update customer.
devon: Enabled temporary fallback. Monitoring shows a 60% reduction in average stream duration within 2 mins. Token deficit trending down.
ops-bot: INFO: fallback policy applied to route /v1/generate on rp-512 at 14:27 UTC.
kevin: After observation window, we'll schedule follow-up to tune burst_tokens and consider a streaming-specific token accounting (e.g., weighted tokens per open stream).
sarah: Noted. I'll send the post-incident note and proposed SLA alignment changes (per-route burst caps, streaming fallbacks, client guidance).
joe-cs: Billing confirmed: no charge for 429s. Customer update drafted and sent. They appreciate the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
maria: Closing loop — incident mitigated by fallback + client guidance. We'll reconvene to adjust pool configs to avoid recurrence.
kevin: Short-lived notes for runbook: include streaming drain checks, monitor long-tail connection percentiles, and have pre-approved fallback toggles for dedicated pools.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: resolved for rp-512 at 14:35 UTC.
